facts: RequestWithBodyArgs accepts body as Record<string, unknown>.
No schema field in this generic PUT surface independently reads or derives the remote current page version.
The conf_put MCP tool uses RequestWithBodyArgs and the createWriteHandler path.
The handler passes caller arguments to handlePut.
Its own documentation example includes a version.number field and states that the version number must be incremented.
handlePut delegates to handleRequest with method PUT.
handleRequest forwards options.body to the Atlassian API service.
For PUT, the service assigns options.body to fetchOptions.body and calls fetchAtlassian.
This pinned path contains no service-layer read-before-write of the current page version.

authoritative_source_evidence.authority: Atlassian official Confluence Cloud REST API v2 reference
facts: PUT /pages/{id} requires a version object in the request body.
A successful page update returns 200 OK.
The documented response set also includes 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, and 404 Not Found.

authoritative_source_evidence.authority: Atlassian official Confluence Cloud REST API v2 OpenAPI
facts: PageUpdateRequest requires id, status, title, body, and version.
version.number is documented as the new version of the updated page.
For a current page, version.number is to be set to the current version number plus one; callers are directed to Get page by id if the current version is unknown.
The admitted OpenAPI does not state an exact stale/non-next version mutation consequence.

open_evidence_limits: Official Atlassian documentation is retrieval-time web evidence rather than an immutable vendor Git object.
The evidence establishes a next-version ordering requirement but not the exact mutation consequence of a stale/non-next supplied version.
The target claim is a static request-realization claim at the pinned MCP revision; no live Confluence deployment conformance is claimed.
